name: PN5321A3HN_C106,55
title: PN532/C1 NFC controller, 13.56 MHz transceiver with 80C51 core
summary: The PN532/C1 is a 13.56 MHz contactless transceiver run by an on-chip 80C51 (40 KB ROM, 1 KB RAM). It works as an ISO/IEC 14443A/MIFARE, ISO/IEC 14443B or FeliCa reader/writer, emulates MIFARE Classic 1K/4K and FeliCa cards, and does ISO/IEC 18092 (NFCIP-1) peer-to-peer at 106, 212 and 424 kbit/s. A host talks to it over SPI, I2C or a high-speed UART chosen by two pins; an internal LDO lets it run straight from a 2.7 to 5.5 V battery, and a switched SVDD output powers a secure IC on its NFC-WI/S2C port.
key_figures: SPI (5 MHz max), I2C (400 kHz), HSU (up to 1.288 Mbit/s)
up to 50 mm typical, antenna dependent

rows: heatsink very thin quad flat, 40 terminals, body 6 x 6 x 0.85 mm, leadless, MSL 2
notes: xx is the ROM code version; each ROM code has its own user manual describing its firmware functions.
Covered by Innovatron's ISO/IEC 14443 Type B patent licence.
MSL 2 rating tested to J-STD-020C (July 2004).

circuits.title: Application diagram
circuits.description: A battery feeds VBAT directly and, through a power management unit, the host's rail, which also supplies PVDD so the host and the PN532's interface pads share one logic level. The LDO output DVDD is wired outside the chip to AVDD and TVDD; DVDD and TVDD each get 4.7 µF X7R/X5R plus 100 nF, AVDD and PVDD 100 nF each. The host drives RSTPD_N, takes P70_IRQ as its interrupt and talks over the host interface pins. The secure core runs from SVDD (100 nF to ground) and links over SIGOUT, SIGIN and P34/SIC_CLK. TX1 and TX2 each drive a 560 nH / 220 pF low-pass filter to the TVSS ground, then series C1 and parallel C2 matching capacitors and a damping resistor RQ into a centre-tapped loop antenna. The receiver takes its signal from the TX1 filter node through 2.7 kΩ and 1 nF; 1 kΩ from RX to VMID biases it, and VMID has 100 nF to ground. A 27.12 MHz crystal with 22 pF at each end sits on OSCIN/OSCOUT; TESTEN is grounded. An optional pair of transistors with 1 kΩ drain resistors, gated by LOADMOD, loads the two antenna ends for card-mode load modulation.
notes: C1 and C2 of the matching network (C10 to C13) range from 10 to 300 pF; RQ is a few ohms.
The host interface pins 27 to 30 take their function from the I0/I1 selection (Host interface selection table).
I0, I1, AUX1, AUX2, P35, P30 to P33 and RSTOUT_N are not wired in this circuit; I0 and I1 choose the host interface.

operation.text: An 80C51 with a 6-clock machine cycle runs the chip from 40 KB of ROM and 1 KB of RAM, with three timers, an interrupt controller, a debug UART on P30/P31 and the GPIO port logic. Its firmware (the ROM code, xx in the part number) sets the host protocol, and a separate user manual covers each ROM code.

The contactless interface unit (CIU) is the 13.56 MHz modem. Reader/writer: ISO/IEC 14443A/MIFARE with full framing, parity and CRC and MIFARE Classic 1K/4K crypto; FeliCa; ISO/IEC 14443B layers 2 and 3 with anticollision left to firmware. Card emulation: MIFARE Classic 1K/4K and FeliCa, load-modulating from the transmitter or from LOADMOD through an outside circuit; full secure card function needs a secure IC on NFC-WI/S2C. NFCIP-1 (ISO/IEC 18092, ECMA 340) peer-to-peer runs active and passive, as initiator or target, at 106, 212 and 424 kbit/s. Higher rates than 424 kbit/s pass through the NFC-WI/S2C pins with external analog parts.
Typical range is up to 50 mm as a reader/writer or in NFCIP-1, and about 100 mm in card emulation, all depending on antenna size, tuning, supply and the outside field strength.

A 64-byte FIFO carries data between the 80C51 and the CIU; there is a CRC co-processor, a programmable timer clocked at 6.78 MHz, a random number generator, a data mode detector that recognises ISO/IEC 14443A, FeliCa and NFCIP-1 signalling, an RF level detector and an antenna presence self test. The most used CIU registers sit in the SFR space.

TX1 and TX2, powered from TVDD and returned to TVSS1/TVSS2, put out the 13.56 MHz carrier (the 27.12 MHz crystal halved) shaped by the modulation envelope, and drive the antenna through a few passive matching and filter parts. The modulation index is set by the driver conductances: p-side by CIU_CWGsP and CIU_ModGsP, n-side by CIU_GsNOn and CIU_GsNOff, and also by antenna design and tuning; about 8 % is the suggested index for FeliCa and NFCIP-1 at 212 and 424 kbit/s. If only one driver is on, the ModGsNOn and CWGsNOn values serve both.

The detector senses an outside RF field at RX, for NFCIP-1 collision avoidance, and can wake the chip or raise an interrupt. Its threshold is a 4-bit field (RFLevel in CIU_RFCfg) with an optional extra amplifier; see the RF level detector table.

For assembly testing, the chip watches the current drawn through its LDO while the transmitter is on. A missing antenna or tuning network raises TVDD current and sets andet_up; a badly connected EMC filter lowers it and sets andet_bot. The high threshold spans about 40 to 150 mA and the low one 5 to 35 mA in total chip current; the result is read from andet_control (610Ch), not a pin. It is specified for VBAT above 5 V and 0 to 40 °C.
Only one host link runs at a time, chosen by I0 and I1 (Host interface selection table). All host pads run from PVDD. A FIFO manager buffers the bytes between the host link and the 80C51.

Master or slave, standard mode (100 kHz) and fast mode (400 kHz); the PN532 is normally the slave. It wakes from power-down on its own address or a general call with write; a general call with read is not supported in hardware. When woken on its own address it may stretch P50_SCL up to 1 ms.

Full-duplex UART up to 1.288 Mbit/s from the 27.12 MHz clock: one start bit, 8 data bits LSB first, 1 or 2 stop bits on receive and 1 to 4 on transmit. A preamble filter holds back bytes until 00 00 FF has been received, re-armed per frame by firmware. A wake-up counter on HSU_RX rising edges wakes the chip from Soft-Power-Down after 5 edges.

Slave only, half duplex, 8-bit, 5 MHz maximum, bytes LSB first. A transfer begins on the falling edge of NSS; the first byte picks a status read, a FIFO read or a FIFO write (SPI operation table) and data bytes follow. During a FIFO write MISO stays low. The host polls the status byte for the READY flag before reading. Clock phase and polarity are set by CPHA and CPOL in SPIcontrol (A9h).

P30 to P35, P70_IRQ, P71 and P72 each take one of four pad modes (GPIO pad modes table); quasi bidirectional is the reset state. An open-drain pin needs an outside pull-up to drive or read a high level. In Hard-Power-Down the ports are cut from their supply rails and forced to quasi bidirectional.

VBAT, from the battery, supplies everything but the host pads; PVDD, from the host's rail, supplies the host pads. The two may come up in any order and either may be present alone. The LDO makes DVDD for the logic and SVDD for the secure IC; DVDD is brought out to feed AVDD and TVDD, and DVDD, AVDD and TVDD are each decoupled. With an interface other than SPI the part runs without PVDD (below 0.4 V), losing only the PVDD-supplied functions, as long as VBAT is 2.7 to 5.5 V and RSTPD_N is between 0.65 × VBAT and 3.6 V.

With RSTPD_N high and PVDD above 1.6 V: above VBAT = 3.4 V, DVDD is held at 3 V and supply bursts up to 400 mV are rejected; from 3.4 V down to 2.5 V DVDD tracks VBAT less an offset that shrinks from 400 mV to 0; from 2.5 V to 2.35 V DVDD equals VBAT; below 2.35 V the chip is in reset. LDO current is a few mA in operation and under 5 µA in reset. In Soft-Power-Down burst rejection is lost: DVDD is 3 V down to VBAT = 3.3 V, then follows VBAT to 2.35 V, with LDO current under 20 µA, then under 7 µA, and under 5 µA in reset.

With the offset off (enoffset = 0), VBAT ripple is not compensated: DVDD is 3 V above VBAT = 3.0 V, equals VBAT from 3.0 V to 2.35 V, and the chip is in reset below 2.35 V. Soft-Power-Down behaves as with the offset.

The LDO loop bandwidth is narrowed to filter VBAT bursts or widened to bring DVDD up fast; it follows the RF level detector (narrow while RF is seen) unless firmware takes control. An overcurrent detector with four thresholds (300, 210, 180, 150 mA) sets a status bit and can interrupt the 80C51.

Register Control_switch_rng (6106h) turns the secure IC supply on (sic_switch_en); off, SVDD is grounded. Above 40 mA a current limiter trips and sets sic_switch_overload. hide_svdd_sig holds the internal SIGIN low and P34 high to keep switching spikes out.

A 27.12 MHz crystal on OSCIN/OSCOUT with a capacitor from each pin to ground is the time base. The CPU clock is 27.12, 13.56 or 6.78 MHz, 6.78 MHz by default; the HSU runs from 27.12 MHz. Crystals such as TAS-3225A, TAS-7 or KSS2F start within 800 µs with a suitable layout.

The power-on reset holds the chip while DVDD is below 2.4 V and begins powering up once it climbs back over; RSTOUT_N then goes high. A drop of DVDD below 2.35 V for longer than 1 ms resets the chip and drives RSTOUT_N low. RSTPD_N low is Hard-Power-Down: chip in reset, RSTOUT_N low, DVDD pulled to ground, ports disconnected, current at its minimum (2 µA max).

Firmware enters it by setting the I/Os for low current (P32_INT0 has e_hd forced high), powering down the CIU, the SVDD switch and the RF level detector when RF wake-up is unused, enabling the wanted wake-up sources, masking other interrupts and finally setting CPU_PD in PCON; all clocks stop and the LDO drops to its low-power state. Current is 40 µA max without and 45 µA max with the RF detector.

Eight enabled sources can wake the chip from Soft-Power-Down: P32_INT0, P33_INT1, an RF field, HSU, I2C or SPI activity, the NFC-WI counters, and GPIRQ from P34, P35, P50_SCL or P71. The CPU clock returns within a time T1 set by the crystal and layout, 2 ms at most with TAS-3225A, TAS-7 or KSS2F.

In Hard-Power-Down nothing in the CIU runs. CIU Power-down (bit in CIU_Command) leaves only the RF level detector and the 27.12 MHz oscillator running, keeps registers and FIFO, can end on an outside field when AutoWakeUp is set, and takes 1024 clocks to leave. Transmitter power-down (Tx1RFEn, Tx2RFEn low) turns off the field while the receiver still answers as an NFCIP-1 target.

A secure IC (such as a smart card chip) connects to SIGIN and SIGOUT, with P34/SIC_CLK as an extra line, all referred to SVDD which the PN532 supplies. SIGIN takes digital FeliCa or ISO/IEC 14443A from the secure IC; SIGOUT sends data and clock to it. This supports a wired card mode from the host and a virtual card mode through the antenna.
